draft.title: Radians
card: One radian is the size of the angle at the centre of a circle when the arc length equals the radius. Radians are a way to measure angles, like degrees.
The circumference is 2πr, so a full turn is 2π radians. This means π radians = 180°.
multiply the degrees by π/180. Example: 60° × π/180 = π/3.
draft.remember: π radians is 180°. Use π/180 to go to radians and 180/π to go to degrees.

a.why: 150 × π/180 = 150π/180 = 5π/6. The option 6π/5 turns the fraction upside down, which would come from using 180/150 instead of 150/180.
a.clue: Multiply by π/180, then simplify the fraction.

b.q: Mia turns a dial through 5π/4 radians. How many degrees is this?
b.why: 5π/4 × 180/π = 5 × 45 = 225°. The option 150° comes from using 5π/6, a different fraction, and 240° is 4π/3, so neither fits 5π/4.
b.clue: Multiply by 180/π so that π cancels.

final.title: Radians
card: One radian is the size of the angle at the centre of a circle when the arc length equals the radius. Radians are a way to measure angles, like degrees.
The circumference is \(2\pi r\), so a full turn is \(2\pi\) radians. This means \(\pi \text{ radians} = 180^{\circ}\).
final.remember: \(\pi\) radians is 180°. Use \(\frac{\pi}{180}\) to go to radians and \(\frac{180}{\pi}\) to go to degrees.

a.why: \(150 \times \frac{\pi}{180} = \frac{150\pi}{180} = \frac{5\pi}{6}\). The option \(\frac{6\pi}{5}\) turns the fraction upside down, which would come from using \(\frac{180}{150}\) instead of \(\frac{150}{180}\).
a.clue: Multiply by \(\frac{\pi}{180}\), then simplify the fraction.

b.q: Mia turns a dial through \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\) radians. How many degrees is this?
b.why: \(\frac{5\pi}{4} \times \frac{180}{\pi} = 5 \times 45 = 225^{\circ}\). The option 150° comes from using \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\), a different fraction, and 240° is \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\), so neither fits \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\).
